narr: Multiple waves of energy passing along a cold front approaching from near the Ohio River resulted in several rounds of prolonged and, at times, heavy rain across northern and western portions of Greenbrier County. In the 48-hour period ending 10 am on the 28th, the northern half of the County had already received between 1.5 to locally 2.5 inches of rainfall from shower and thunderstorm activity. Snow pack prior to the arrival of the rainfall was confined to the highest elevations of the western half of the county, where 2 to locally 4 inches was on the ground. By the morning of the 28th, soils were almost completely saturated, resulting in efficient runoff of rainfall from showers and thunderstorms that would occur during the evening.
ev: A line of thunderstorms brought at least an inch of rain over a short period of time, which fell across soil that was already saturated from rainfall during the previous 36 hours. Runoff from the rainfall caused the Meadow River to quickly rise out of banks, cutting off portions of Anjean Road, making the road impassible until the flood waters receded. Key Impacts: flooded and impassible roadways; transportation delays.
